sections.h2: Is a cash sale or a listing better for a Colonie house?
sections.html:
It depends on what the house needs and how quickly you must move. Colonie is the most populous suburb of Albany, and plenty of owners there list the traditional way. Deferred repairs, tenants, a probate delay or a tax problem point toward a cash buyer who takes the house as-is.

A listing means preparing the house, scheduling showings and waiting on a buyer's lender. A cash sale replaces that with a walkthrough and a closing date you help choose. The price is usually lower than a top-dollar listing, so total up what each route leaves after the mortgage payoff, back taxes and closing costs before you decide.

  • List with an agent for a house that shows well and a schedule with room in it.
  • Sell without an agent if you have a buyer in hand and can manage the contract.
  • Take a cash offer for an inherited house, a rental with problem tenants, a damaged property or a relocation with a firm date.

sections.h2: What is the Town of Colonie like, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Colonie sits north of Albany, with the Mohawk River along its northern line and the Hudson on the east. Interstates 87, 787 and 90 and US Route 9 cross it, and Albany International Airport lies inside the town. Roughly 56 square miles of land make up the town, which contains two incorporated villages, Colonie and Menands, plus hamlets such as Latham, Loudonville, Newtonville, Boght Corners, Verdoy and West Albany.

The town was formed in 1895 when residents of Watervliet resisted a state plan to turn that whole town into a city. Much of the central area once held Shaker farms, and postwar suburban building took off from there. The population rose from 29,522 in 1950 to 52,760 in 1960 and 69,147 in 1970. The Census Bureau counted 85,590 residents in 2020 and estimates 86,837 for July 1, 2025.

sections.h2: Which school districts and parks come with a Colonie address?
sections.html:
Six public school districts serve the town: South Colonie, North Colonie, Watervliet, Menands, Niskayuna and Mohonasen. South Colonie covers much of the west, including West Albany and the village of Colonie, while North Colonie, which feeds Shaker High School, serves Latham and most of Loudonville and Newtonville. Siena College is in Loudonville.

The Town's own description highlights the 130-acre Crossings park with its trails, a town park with a pool, a 36-hole golf course and a bike trail along the Mohawk. The Casparus F. Pruyn House in Newtonville serves as a cultural center. When you list or sell, name the district and the nearest park, because Colonie buyers shop by both. The Town also operates the Mohawk River Park and Pool Complex and a Parks and Recreation program that it publicizes through a new online parks portal, a detail worth passing along to a family relocating from outside the Capital Region.

sections.h2: When are Colonie property tax bills due?
sections.html:
The Receiver of Taxes mails the general tax bill on December 31, and it is payable in January without penalty. Colonie is a town of the first class, and its collector is an elected Receiver of Taxes and Assessments.

  • General bill: due January 1 to 31, then 1% in February and 2% in March.
  • April 1: unpaid general bills go to the Albany County Department of Finance.
  • School bills: mailed August 31, due in September, then 4% in October.
  • November 1: unpaid school bills go to the county, and after December 1 they move onto the next general bill with a 7% penalty.

The office collects school tax for five districts and also bills water for Latham Water, about 22,000 accounts twice a year, with a 5% penalty after 30 days. One detail matters to sellers and buyers alike: if a prior owner received an exemption they no longer qualified for, an exemption payback charge can show up on the bill. Ask the office for a duplicate bill and any open balance before closing. Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, and live in a one, two or three family house can name a third party to receive duplicate bills on form RP-923, which helps when an aging parent is selling. Counter hours stretch to 6 p.m. during the last five business days of January and September. The Town's page for the 2026 bills gave the penalty-free window as December 31, 2025 through February 2, 2026, so a January 31 that falls on a weekend pushes the deadline to the following Monday.

sections.h2: What do Colonie assessments, grievances and STAR look like for a seller?
sections.html:
The Assessor's office in Memorial Town Hall, 534 New Loudon Road in Latham, runs the standard New York calendar. Exemptions and the taxable status date fall on March 1, the tentative roll is filed May 1, Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May and the final roll is filed July 1.

A complaint must reach the office by 8:00 p.m. on Grievance Day. A postmark that day does not count, and electronic service is refused. Colonie asks owners to come with a recent purchase contract, sales of similar homes nearby or a current appraisal, and the owner carries the burden of proof. The 2026 deadline has passed, so the next one is the fourth Tuesday of May 2027.

Owners who bought after March 2, 2015, or never claimed STAR on a primary home, are told to register for the STAR credit, which pays by check. The Town notes that the Basic STAR income limit is $250,000, and above that you need the credit. A buyer in that group should register after closing, and exemption forms are handed out at the Assessor's counter on weekdays during business hours.

sections.h2: Where are Colonie deeds recorded, and what local notices matter now?
sections.html:
Albany County records deeds and mortgages, and its Clerk reports that deed and mortgage records since 1980 are searchable online. New York's transfer tax is $2 per $500 of consideration. Sellers normally bear it, and Form TP-584 reaches the county clerk within 15 days of deed delivery. Confirm current recording fees with the clerk.

The official Town website is now townofcolonie.gov; the old colonie.org address was replaced on December 5, 2025 after changes in state law, so use the new one when you look up departments. The Town's August 2026 notice also pointed residents to a state damage self-report tool for the rain event of July 29, 2026. If your house took water that day, ask the Town whether that tool is still open before you commit to a buyer or sign disclosures.

faqs.q: Will a cash buyer take a Colonie house with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Many will, but terms differ, so say so up front. Tell the buyer the lease dates, rent and deposit, and check your lease before you sign anything.

faqs.q: When is a Colonie property tax payment late?
faqs.a: After January 31. February adds 1% and March adds 2%, and on April 1 unpaid general bills go to the Albany County Department of Finance.

faqs.q: Does Colonie handle school taxes at Town Hall?
faqs.a: Yes for five districts. The Receiver of Taxes collects South Colonie, North Colonie, Menands, Niskayuna and Mohonasen bills, which are mailed August 31 and due in September.

faqs.q: What is the next Grievance Day in Colonie?
faqs.a: The fourth Tuesday in May 2027, which is May 25. Complaints must be in the Assessor's office by 8:00 p.m. that day, and exemption forms are due March 1.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Colonie deed?
faqs.a: The Albany County Clerk. Bring Form TP-584 with the deed, and ask the clerk about current fees.
